resolution.note: operator-inbox dispose --task and search read the task store (pending, tasks/, archive); regression test/claude/operator-inbox-dispose.test.ts red on base, green on branch

title: Operator inbox dispose accepts a pending task id
body:
Source: lead session 2026-11-20 closing t-ak5f21v: `node scripts/claude/operator-inbox.ts dispose <hash> --task t-ak5f21v` failed with "FAIL t-ak5f21v: no tasks/t-ak5f21v.json" while `krn task show` and `krn task close` handled the same pending record (refs/krn/pending-tasks). The prompts were disposed with --answered instead.
Evidence: src/successor/operator-inbox.ts:112-116 checks only `tasks/<id>.json`; src/task/pending.ts:212 `isPendingId` and src/task/store.ts:222 already read pending records.
Fix: accept a task id that has a tasks/ record or a pending record (one task reader, not a second guess of the store), with a regression test at the lowest layer (KRN-14).
Also file with this PR: `krn standards propose --kind prose --text "A wait that can return before its condition holds (a check-in, a timeout) is followed by a check of the condition itself; its exit code alone never means done." --evidence .krn/runs/lead/host-eval/report.md` (lesson: `hc wait --output` returned 0 at its 180 s check-in while the T3 arm still ran).
Outcome: `operator-inbox.ts dispose <hash> --task <pending id>` exits 0 and prints `disposed <hash>` (base: exit 1, "no tasks/<id>.json").
Proof: the new test fails on the base and passes on the branch.
